question.problem:
Consider the triangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(-1,0),(0,-1)$ and $(1,1),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ According to Green's theorem, 

$$
{∮}_{C}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2xy)\,dx+2{sin}^{2}⁡(xy)\,dy={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14120089/assets/f4bb6636c104cf17bcd4b25037a3490ba30b7c1380b152c33504d9015903bdca.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2xy)$ and $Q(x,y)=2{sin}^{2}⁡xy.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy),\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=4y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)=2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2xy)\,dx+2{sin}^{2}⁡(xy)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy)-(-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy)))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy)+2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2(x+y)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy)\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)=2(x+y)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2xy).$
